checks: Exploded offsets do not change attachment metadata.

defaults.rationale: Illustrative display offsets: the cited synovial-joint section supports what the menisci do (claim.knee-layer-peel) but gives no layer thickness, no joint dimension and no separation distance, so every number below is an authored presentation choice and none describes anatomy. The schedule is deliberately linear in layer index so the expected offset of any layer is a single multiplication a check can verify, and so reset is exactly the t = 0 case rather than a separate code path. The ordering is outermost to innermost because that is the order a peel reveals them. Tunable: step size and layer count are free; what must not change is that the offset is composed with an immutable rest transform rather than written into it.

layer_order.note: authored teaching order; the structure IDs themselves come from the sourced mesh

peel_amount.note: authored; 0 is the assembled reference state, 1 is fully peeled

per_layer_offset_step.note: authored display separation per layer index at full peel; a display distance, not a tissue thickness

offset_direction.value: each layer's outward normal at its own rest pose
offset_direction.note: authored; fixed at rest so the explosion does not rotate with the camera

layer_thicknesses.note: the cited section gives no anatomical thickness for any of these layers

joint_dimensions.note: supply them with the mesh and its own source

equations: offset_i = i * per_layer_offset_step * peel_amount, with i the layer index from 0 for the innermost visible layer
world_transform_i = rest_transform_i composed with translate(offset_i * normal_i)
reset is peel_amount = 0, which makes every offset exactly 0

worked_example.inputs: The 5 authored layers with a 0.03 m step, peeled to peel_amount = 1.0 and then reset to 0.0
worked_example.expected: Offsets 0, 0.03, 0.06, 0.09 and 0.12 m, total spread 0.12 m between the innermost and outermost layer and 0.30 m of offset summed over all layers; after reset every layer's world transform equals its rest transform exactly, with a maximum component difference of 0.0 rather than a small residue, and every attachment record is byte-identical before and after
worked_example.derivation: offset_i = i x 0.03 x 1.0 for i = 0..4 gives 0, 0.03, 0.06, 0.09, 0.12 m; the sum is 0.30 m and the spread is the largest minus the smallest, 0.12 m. At peel_amount = 0 every term contains the factor 0, so the composed translation is the identity and the world transform is the rest transform itself - an exact equality, not a tolerance. That is the discriminating check: an implementation that accumulates the offset into the stored rest transform instead of composing with it will drift away from equality after peeling and resetting several times, and will fail this comparison even though a screenshot looks correct.

tolerance.reset_exactness: exact equality of the reset transform with the rest transform; use an identity comparison, not an epsilon
tolerance.offset_m: 1e-9 m on a computed offset against the formula
tolerance.attachment_metadata: unchanged: compare the attachment records before and after, not just the geometry
